agent_based_model.summary: Trend followers, mean reverters, informed and noise traders and a liquidity provider trade forward from each bar; the share of simulated paths that end higher is P(up).
agent_based_model.implementationNote: Bridge: P(up) is the share of simulated paths ending higher, through a logistic curve fitted on validation. Differs from the spec: one instrument; type proportions, impact, noise and tail are calibrated by CMA-ES (method of simulated moments) and informed agents read a ridge index of the features. Expect: calibrated to train-span bar moments; directional edge is near the base rate.

agent_population_size.label: Agents per type
agent_population_size.description: How many heterogeneous agents of each type trade (each with its own lookback and sensitivity).

trend_follower_lookback_bars.label: Trend lookback (bars)
trend_follower_lookback_bars.description: The longest lookback a trend-following agent reads (agents draw theirs up to it).

mean_reversion_window_bars.label: Reversion window (bars)
mean_reversion_window_bars.description: The longest moving-average window a mean-reverting agent reads.

liquidity_inventory_aversion.label: Liquidity provider inventory aversion
liquidity_inventory_aversion.description: The share of the accumulated price impact the liquidity provider works off every bar.

factor_ridge_penalty.label: Factor ridge penalty
factor_ridge_penalty.description: Ridge penalty (a share of the bar count) of the linear index that maps the features to the drift or the information agents read.

path_count.label: Simulated paths
path_count.description: How many future paths are simulated for every bar; the share that ends higher is the raw P(up).

iteration_count.label: Calibration generations
iteration_count.description: CMA-ES generations of the method-of-simulated-moments calibration.

population_size.label: Calibration population

maximum_training_bars.label: Maximum training bars
maximum_training_bars.description: The most recent training bars the generator is fitted on.

multi_agent_simulation.summary: A market maker, a trend follower, a mean reverter and an informed trader learn their policies by Q-learning, then trade forward from each bar; the share of simulated paths that end higher is P(up).
multi_agent_simulation.implementationNote: Bridge: P(up) is the share of simulated paths ending higher, through a logistic curve fitted on validation. Differs from the spec: four independent tabular Q-learners trained on replayed train-span moves plus their own impact; the flow-to-move link is a train-span least-squares fit; independent learners reach no equilibrium. Expect: calibrated to train-span bar moments; directional edge is near the base rate.

episode_count.label: Episodes
episode_count.description: Training episodes, run in parallel batches of a tenth each.

episode_length_bars.label: Episode length (bars)
episode_length_bars.description: Consecutive training bars one episode replays.

learning_rate.label: Learning rate
learning_rate.description: Step size of each Q-value update.

discount_factor.label: Discount factor
discount_factor.description: Weight of the next bar's value in a Q-value.

exploration_rate.label: Exploration rate
exploration_rate.description: Share of training actions taken at random instead of greedily.

bin_count.label: Signal bins
bin_count.description: Train-quantile bins of each agent's own signal (its states).

impact_coefficient.label: Training impact per contract
impact_coefficient.description: Price impact of one contract of net order flow in the training environment (move-scale units).

trend_follower_lookback_bars.label: Trend lookback (bars)
trend_follower_lookback_bars.description: The longest lookback a trend-following agent reads (agents draw theirs up to it).

mean_reversion_window_bars.label: Reversion window (bars)
mean_reversion_window_bars.description: The longest moving-average window a mean-reverting agent reads.

factor_ridge_penalty.label: Factor ridge penalty
factor_ridge_penalty.description: Ridge penalty (a share of the bar count) of the linear index that maps the features to the drift or the information agents read.

path_count.label: Simulated paths
path_count.description: How many future paths are simulated for every bar; the share that ends higher is the raw P(up).

maximum_training_bars.label: Maximum training bars
maximum_training_bars.description: The most recent training bars the generator is fitted on.

markov_chain_monte_carlo.summary: A Bayesian Student-t model of the h-bar move is sampled by adaptive random-walk Metropolis-Hastings; P(up) is the posterior-predictive probability of a rise.
markov_chain_monte_carlo.implementationNote: Bridge: P(up) is the posterior-predictive mean of P(move > 0), through a validation-fitted curve. Differs from the spec: the sampled model is a Student-t regression of the h-bar move on the first principal components; own adaptive Metropolis-Hastings, arviz R-hat, and a fit with R-hat above 1.05 is refused. Overlapping targets make the posterior too narrow. Expect: close to a regularised linear model.

iteration_count.label: Iterations per chain
iteration_count.description: Metropolis-Hastings iterations of every chain, burn-in included.

burn_in_fraction.label: Burn-in fraction
burn_in_fraction.description: Share of each chain discarded while the proposal adapts.

thinning_interval.label: Thinning interval
thinning_interval.description: Every how many iterations a draw is kept.

principal_component_count.label: Principal components
principal_component_count.description: How many principal components of the features describe a bar's state.

target_acceptance_rate.label: Target acceptance rate
target_acceptance_rate.description: The acceptance rate the proposal scale adapts toward during burn-in.

student_degrees_of_freedom.label: Student-t degrees of freedom
student_degrees_of_freedom.description: Tail weight of the move likelihood (lower is heavier).

chain_starting_dispersion.label: Chain starting dispersion
chain_starting_dispersion.description: How many standard errors from the least-squares fit the chains start.

maximum_training_bars.label: Maximum training bars
maximum_training_bars.description: The most recent training bars the generator is fitted on.

monte_carlo_simulation.summary: Future paths are bootstrapped in blocks from the moves that followed the most similar training bars; the share that ends higher is P(up).
monte_carlo_simulation.implementationNote: Bridge: P(up) is the share of bootstrapped paths ending higher, through a logistic curve fitted on validation. Differs from the spec: paths are moving-block resamples of the one-bar steps that followed the nearest training bars in principal-component space (a nearest-neighbour analogue with resampled uncertainty), not draws from assumed distributions. Expect: a modest edge where the feature state recurs.

path_count.label: Simulated paths
path_count.description: How many future paths are simulated for every bar; the share that ends higher is the raw P(up).

neighbor_count.label: Neighbours
neighbor_count.description: Nearest training bars whose following moves are resampled.

block_length_bars.label: Block length (bars)
block_length_bars.description: Consecutive steps copied per block (capped at the horizon).

principal_component_count.label: Principal components
principal_component_count.description: How many principal components of the features describe a bar's state.

maximum_training_bars.label: Maximum training bars
maximum_training_bars.description: The most recent training bars the generator is fitted on.

discrete_event_simulation.summary: Up and down tick events follow a self-exciting Hawkes process fitted by maximum likelihood; Ogata thinning simulates the events of the next bars and the share of paths that end higher is P(up).
discrete_event_simulation.implementationNote: Bridge: P(up) is the share of simulated event paths ending higher, through a validation-fitted curve. Differs from the spec: a Hawkes process on bar close-to-close tick moves (events spaced evenly inside a bar), because tick history covers only a few days and intrabar highs and lows are not available at prediction; Ogata thinning, no queues. Expect: calibrated to train-span bar moments; directional edge is near the base rate.

path_count.label: Simulated paths
path_count.description: How many future paths are simulated for every bar; the share that ends higher is the raw P(up).

events_per_bar.label: Events per bar
events_per_bar.description: Average events per bar the event size is set for (a bar's move in events).

memory_bars.label: Excitation memory (bars)
memory_bars.description: Past bars whose events excite the intensity at the start of a simulation.

hawkes_branching_limit.label: Branching limit
hawkes_branching_limit.description: Upper bound of the branching matrix's spectral radius (the events one event triggers, all generations); keeps the process stationary.

horizon_event_limit.label: Thinning step limit
horizon_event_limit.description: Most thinning steps one simulation takes before it stops.

principal_component_count.label: Principal components
principal_component_count.description: How many principal components of the features describe a bar's state.

iteration_count.label: Likelihood iterations
iteration_count.description: L-BFGS-B iterations of the maximum-likelihood fit.

maximum_training_bars.label: Maximum training bars
maximum_training_bars.description: The most recent training bars the generator is fitted on.

event_driven_simulation.summary: A typed event queue (market, signal, order, fill) replays rule strategies over the training span with slippage and costs; the best strategy's signal gives P(up).
event_driven_simulation.implementationNote: Bridge: P(up) is the kept rule strategy's signal through a logistic curve fitted on validation. Differs from the spec: the event queue (market, signal, order and fill with slippage and cost) replays 96 rule strategies over the train span and keeps the best net Sharpe; the predictive content is only the wrapped rule strategy. Expect: probabilities near the base rate unless a simple momentum or reversion rule works.

slippage_ticks.label: Slippage (ticks)
slippage_ticks.description: Adverse ticks every simulated fill pays on top of the cost model.

maximum_training_bars.label: Maximum training bars
maximum_training_bars.description: The most recent training bars the generator is fitted on.

stochastic_differential_equation.summary: Geometric Brownian motion, an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck drift factor, Heston stochastic variance or Merton jumps are fitted on the training span and simulated by Euler-Maruyama; the share of paths that end higher is P(up).
stochastic_differential_equation.implementationNote: Bridge: P(up) is the share of Euler-Maruyama paths ending higher, through a logistic curve fitted on validation. Differs from the spec: the drift is a one-factor Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process on a ridge index of the features (geometric Brownian motion has no conditioning); Heston and Merton change the spread more than the direction. Expect: calibrated to train-span bar moments; directional edge is near the base rate.

diffusion_model.label: Diffusion model
diffusion_model.description: Which stochastic differential equation is simulated.

path_count.label: Simulated paths
path_count.description: How many future paths are simulated for every bar; the share that ends higher is the raw P(up).

discretization_steps_per_bar.label: Euler steps per bar
discretization_steps_per_bar.description: Euler-Maruyama steps each bar is split into.

factor_ridge_penalty.label: Factor ridge penalty
factor_ridge_penalty.description: Ridge penalty (a share of the bar count) of the linear index that maps the features to the drift or the information agents read.

variance_window_bars.label: Variance window (bars)
variance_window_bars.description: Bars of residuals the Heston variance starts from and is fitted in blocks of.

jump_threshold_deviations.label: Jump threshold (robust deviations)
jump_threshold_deviations.description: A Merton training residual beyond this many robust deviations is a jump.

system_dynamics.summary: Momentum pressure, stretch from a moving average, volatility and an information inflow are stocks joined by flows with a delayed feedback loop; the projected displacement over the horizon gives P(up).
system_dynamics.implementationNote: Bridge: P(up) is the stock-and-flow model's projected displacement through a logistic curve fitted on validation. Differs from the spec: stocks measured from bars (momentum pressure, stretch read with a delay, volatility) plus a ridge information inflow; flows fitted to train-span trajectories by differential evolution; deterministic. Expect: calibrated to train-span bar moments; directional edge is near the base rate.

pressure_span_bars.label: Pressure span (bars)
pressure_span_bars.description: Span of the weighted mean of steps that is the pressure stock.

stretch_window_bars.label: Stretch window (bars)
stretch_window_bars.description: Moving-average window the stretch stock is measured from.

feedback_delay_bars.label: Feedback delay (bars)
feedback_delay_bars.description: How late the stretch feeds back into the price flow.

discretization_steps_per_bar.label: Euler steps per bar
discretization_steps_per_bar.description: Euler integration steps each bar is split into.

iteration_count.label: Evolution generations
iteration_count.description: Differential-evolution generations of the flow fit.

population_size.label: Evolution population
population_size.description: Candidate parameter sets per differential-evolution generation.

flow_sensitivity_bound.label: Flow sensitivity bound
flow_sensitivity_bound.description: Largest absolute value a flow coefficient may take.

factor_ridge_penalty.label: Factor ridge penalty
factor_ridge_penalty.description: Ridge penalty (a share of the bar count) of the linear index that maps the features to the drift or the information agents read.
